For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smartsheet is looking for a Principal Pricing Program & Operations Manager to join our Pricing & Packaging team. This individual connects pricing strategy to execution. Our pricing analysts and strategists develop the research, analysis, and recommendations. You will take those recommendations and drive them to realization: building the plan, aligning the stakeholders, and landing the change across Product, Sales, Finance, Marketing, Legal, Billing, and Operations.

You will work with guidance from the Sr. Director of Pricing & Packaging, but you will own the execution of your programs end to end. You will keep multiple initiatives moving at once, adapt quickly as priorities shift, and make sure that what we decide in the pricing team is what customers and the field actually experience. This is a high-impact role for someone who combines strong B2B SaaS pricing acumen with the discipline of a program and operations leader. You understand why a pricing change is the right call, and you know how to get it done.

You will report to our Sr. Director of Packaging & Pricing, and you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer.

What You Will Do:

Program execution

• Own the end-to-end execution of pricing and packaging initiatives, from the handoff of a recommendation through launch and post-launch measurement. Examples include new packaging constructs, list price changes, rate card updates, AI and new-capability monetization, and customer migrations.

• Build and manage detailed program plans, timelines, dependencies, risk registers, and RACI structures across multiple concurrent projects.

• Translate pricing recommendations into clear requirements and action plans for the teams that implement them, including Product, Engineering, Sales Ops, Finance, Billing, Legal, Marketing, and Customer Success.

• Run program cadences, including stand-ups, steering committees, and executive updates. Surface risks and decisions early, and escalate with clear options and trade-offs.

• Re-plan and re-prioritize quickly as business priorities, market conditions, and leadership direction change.

Cross-functional leadership and communication

• Build trusted partnerships across the organization and secure stakeholder buy-in, often without direct authority.

• Write clear, executive-ready documents, including program briefs, decision memos, launch plans, FAQs, and status reports.

• Present program status, outcomes, and recommendations to senior stakeholders and leadership.

• Partner with Sales Enablement and Marketing to develop field-facing materials such as pricing guides, discounting guidelines, talk tracks, and training, so that changes are understood and adopted.

Pricing operations and governance

• Operationalize pricing policy by partnering with the right cross-functional partners for critical changes to prices, discount guidelines, approval workflows, quoting and CPQ configuration, billing and systems changes, and exception handling.

• Contribute to pricing governance, including intake, prioritization, decision rights, approvals, and deal-desk escalation paths.

• Build repeatable playbooks, templates, and processes for pricing launches, migrations, and changes so the team can scale.

• Partner with Finance, Revenue Operations, and Business Systems to ensure pricing changes are accurately reflected in systems, reporting, and forecasts.

Analytics and performance tracking

• Define success metrics for each program and track post-launch performance, including ARR, NRR, ARPU, attach rate, price realization, discount levels, and migration performance.

• Use data to monitor adoption, identify issues, and recommend corrective actions or follow-on work.

• Work with the pricing team to understand the research, models, and assumptions behind each recommendation so you can execute with context and flag when results diverge from the plan.

• Support competitive pricing and packaging monitoring that informs ongoing program decisions.

You Have:

• 7 to 10+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, revenue operations, strategy and operations, program management, or a related commercial function, with at least 5 years in B2B SaaS pricing or monetization.

• A proven track record of driving pricing or packaging changes to execution in a multi-product, multi-segment SaaS business, not only recommending them. You can point to launches or migrations you delivered and the outcomes they produced.

• Strong program and project management skills. You are skilled at managing complex, cross-functional initiatives with many dependencies and stakeholders. 

• Operations experience, such as pricing operations, deal desk, revenue operations, sales operations, or business operations, and familiarity with how pricing flows through quoting, billing, and finance systems.

• Strong business and pricing strategy acumen. You understand value metrics, packaging architecture, unit economics, and how pricing decisions affect revenue, margin, and customer experience.

• Excellent verbal and written communication. You can distill complex topics into clear narratives for executives, partners, and the field.

• Comfort working cross-functionally, with the ability to influence and build consensus across teams with different priorities.

• The ability to adapt and pivot quickly. You stay organized and focused as priorities change, and you bring structure to ambiguity.

• Analytical skills sufficient to size impacts and track results: advanced Excel or Sheets, working knowledge of SQL, and experience with a BI tool (e.g., Tableau).

• A collaborative, low-ego working style that fits Smartsheet's culture.

Nice to Have:

• Experience in work management, collaboration, productivity, or analytics SaaS, ideally with AI-enhanced products.

• Experience launching or operationalizing pricing for AI features.

• Exposure to PLG plus enterprise "hybrid GTM" environments.

• Experience managing customer migrations, grandfathering, or renewal-based price changes.

• Hands-on familiarity with CPQ, billing, and CRM systems and the processes that surround them.

• Background in pricing consulting or strategy consulting.

• Experience with pricing governance forums.

• Global pricing experience (US plus EMEA/APAC).

About Sarvam
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC.

About the role
Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets and rate-limiting all part of the same stack.
We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done.

What you will do

Own a platform area end to end
• Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them.
• Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs.
• Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes.
• Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome.
• Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance.
• Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability.

Build real-time and model-serving pipelines
• Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation.
• Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR.
• Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes.

Think in systems and from first principles
• Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation.
• Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone.
• Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot.
• Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly.

Raise the bar for the team
• Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs.
• Partner with the Inference and MLOps teams on making model serving fast, reliable and operable.
• Mentor junior engineers through RFC reviews, code review and pairing.
• Practice design-first, documentation-first engineering: RFCs before code, no tribal knowledge.

What we are looking for
• 4–6 years of building and operating production backend systems.
• At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed.
• Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes.
• Experience with low-latency or high-throughput services, and comfort reasoning about p95 and p99 latency.
• Solid fundamentals with a relational database and a cache, such as PostgreSQL and Redis: schema design, query performance and caching strategy.
• Fluency in at least one backend language and willingness to work in both Python and Golang.
• Experience running services with containers, CI/CD and production monitoring.
• Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with concrete examples of what you automated or sped up.
• A bias for action: fast on reversible decisions, careful on irreversible ones.
• Clear writing, especially RFCs and design docs that others can act on.

Good to have (not required)
• Voice AI or real-time audio experience: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming ASR or TTS, or audio processing with FFmpeg or pyav, codecs, sample rates and VAD.
• Production experience in Go, or in Python with FastAPI.
• Experience serving LLM, ASR, TTS or vision models in production.
• Experience building metering, billing, wallet or payments infrastructure.
• Running services on Kubernetes in production.
• Time at an early- or growth-stage startup.

Why Sarvam
• A fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, with real population-scale impact.
• Researchers, engineers, builders and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.
• High ownership and high impact from day one.

About Nivoda
Nivoda is the operating system for the global jewellery industry. Our B2B marketplace connects jewellery retailers with diamond, gemstone and jewellery suppliers in 70+ countries, and we process $300M+ in annual transactions in a $350B industry that has barely been touched by technology.
We remove the traditional barriers of capital, geography and information asymmetry. An independent jeweller in Ohio can source from a cutter in Mumbai with the same ease, pricing and confidence as one of the world's largest chains. That's the whole point.

Our Mission 🚀
Diamond and gemstone trading has run on inefficiency, opacity and exclusivity for generations. Relationships were gatekept, pricing was hidden, and the size of your business decided the terms you got. We're building the infrastructure that changes that — so any jewellery business, anywhere, regardless of size, can compete on the quality of what they do rather than who they know.

The Marketing Team ⭐️
We're a remote-first, low-hierarchy company where the best idea wins. Marketing at Nivoda is at an inflection point: we have real product-market fit, thousands of businesses transacting, a category we have the opportunity to redefine, and a marketing function that has not yet been built to match the scale of the opportunity.

About the Role 
We're hiring a VP of Growth to build Nivoda's marketing function from the ground up and turn it into a predictable growth engine for a two-sided global marketplace.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's or maintainer’s. You'll own the strategy, the growth model, the budget, the team and the number. You'll be the person who decides what Nivoda's category story is in partnership with the CEO, how we reach tens of thousands of independent jewellers and suppliers, and how we prove — with data, not decks — which of those bets are working.
You'll report directly to the President and sit on the senior leadership team, with a mandate that spans demand generation, product marketing, brand, content, lifecycle and marketing operations across every market we trade in.

What would you be doing? 
• 
Owning Nivoda's marketing strategy end to end - translating company goals into a growth model, then into the channels, programmes and headcount that deliver it
• 
Building the marketing team from its current base: hiring, structuring and levelling up a global team, and building the systems, briefs and feedback loops that make good marketers great
• 
Owning demand generation and pipeline contribution for both sides of the marketplace - retailers who need supply, and suppliers who need demand
• 
Building the measurement layer: attribution, funnel instrumentation, CAC and payback by segment and geography, and a reporting rhythm the leadership team actually trusts
• 
Running marketing as a portfolio of experiments rather than a calendar of campaigns - defining leading indicators, killing what doesn't work quickly, and going all-in on what does
•
